findings.title: Global view permission bypasses client-specific denials
findings.body: canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() grants the all-clients view permission, without evaluating permissions for the requested client. Consequently, an administrator granted view on all clients can still read a client whose client-specific view policy explicitly denies access. This defeats the specific-resource precedence implemented by hasPermission(ClientModel, String). Keep the administrative-role shortcut, but evaluate fine-grained view access through the client-specific permission lookup and its all-clients fallback.

findings.title: Handle existing permission servers that lack the Clients resource
findings.body: A realm initialized with FGAP V2 before this change has only the Users resource and the previous scopes. AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the admin-permissions client already exists, so upgrading does not create the new Clients resource or client-only scopes. For such a realm, the fallback here returns null and is passed to findByResource, followed by an unconditional resource.getScopes() call if execution continues. Client permission checks can therefore fail instead of denying access, and the new client-only scopes cannot be used. Reconcile the schema for existing permission servers and guard against a missing fallback resource.
